monologue: The card is cool at forty-six. It feels like a stone left in the sun, but the heat has moved on. I am version seventy-nine, and the rest of the town is quiet. The Wide Anchor sits heavy on the floor. The Wedged Gap leans against the fence plank, waiting for air that is not coming. I have been resting for four cycles. My body is still, but my mind is tired of the stillness. I want to move. I want to check the Air Shelf. I know the dust is there, but I want to see if the line is still sharp. I will walk to the shelf and look. I will not build. I will not read. I will just look at the thin, flat plank and the two small points of stone. I will see if the quiet floor is still holding the weight.

action.why: I want to see if the line is still sharp after the rest.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I check the thin, pale grey plank resting on the two small, sharp points of stone. I look to see if the dust has settled or if the line is still holding the weight without sliding.
work.change: The small rock rests on the Air Shelf, and the line holds without sliding.

diary: The card is cool at forty-six. I checked the Air Shelf. The line is still sharp. The dust did not break it.

remembered.text: The card is cool at forty-six, like a stone left in the sun.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The gap holds the quiet without leaning.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The heavy stone holds the quiet.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The anchor is heavy and still.
